module_title: North-East Passes, The Ghats, and the Highest Roads
introduction: At the advanced level, examiners target the passes of Arunachal Pradesh, the passes (Ghats) of the Western Ghats in South India, and the world records held by Ladakh's motorable roads.

core_concepts.title: Passes of Arunachal Pradesh
core_concepts.description:
1. **Bomdi La:** Connects Arunachal Pradesh to Lhasa (the capital of Tibet). 
2. **Diphu Pass:** Situated at the strategic **tri-junction** of India (Arunachal Pradesh), China, and Myanmar. 
3. **Yonggyap Pass:** The Brahmaputra River enters India (Arunachal Pradesh) near this pass.

core_concepts.title: World's Highest Motorable Roads
core_concepts.description:
1. **Umling La:** **Ladakh**. Situated at an elevation of 19,024 feet, it is currently the **world's highest motorable road** (built by BRO). 
2. **Khardung La:** **Ladakh**. It formerly held the record. It connects Leh to the Nubra Valley.

core_concepts.title: Vital Passes of the Western Ghats (South India)
core_concepts.description:
In South India, mountain passes are referred to as 'Ghats' or 'Gaps':
1. **Thal Ghat:** Maharashtra. Connects **Mumbai to Nashik**. 
2. **Bhor Ghat:** Maharashtra. Connects **Mumbai to Pune**. 
3. **Palakkad Gap (Pal Ghat):** Connects **Kerala (Palakkad) to Tamil Nadu (Coimbatore)**. It is situated between the Nilgiri and Anamalai hills.

core_concepts.title: Peaks of the Islands and Eastern Ghats
core_concepts.description:
1. **Saddle Peak:** The highest peak of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (located in North Andaman). 
2. **Jindhagada Peak:** Andhra Pradesh. It is the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats.

important_entities.name: Mount Saramati
important_entities.significance: It is the highest peak in Nagaland and acts as a natural barrier on the India-Myanmar border.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
The Hardest Exam Trap: Students constantly mix up which pass connects Mumbai to Pune and which connects Mumbai to Nashik. 
Trick: 'Munna brings the Thali' (Mu=Mumbai, Nna=Nashik -> Thali=Thal Ghat). And to travel from Mumbai to Pune, you must leave at 'Bhor' (Dawn) -> Bhor Ghat.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Passes of Arunachal Pradesh: Bo = Bomdi La, Di = Diphu, Ya = Yonggyap.

exam_strategy_tips: A highly repeated question in NDA/CDS and SSC CGL: 'The Palghat gap connects which of the following states?' Answer: Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
